messages.subject: [Basta-users] Obtaining posterior values from iterations
messages.body_plain:
Hey BaSTA users,

I would like to look at and plot the posterior distributions using the simulation results not just the estimates provided in the coefficient table, similar to the posterior distributions in Fig.5 in Colchero & Clark 2012, which appears to incorporate the asymmetry of the results.

Does BaSTA save the individual iterations for manual plotting and calculations?

Thanks

Jenni

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Jennifer Graham
PhD Researcher
Centre for Ecology and Conservation
University of Exeter, Cornwall Campus
Tremough
Penryn
Cornwall
TR10 9EZ

messages.subject: [Basta-users] Obtaining posterior values from iterations
messages.body_plain:
Dear Jenni,

If you have a basta object called "out", you can access the parameter traces (which are the individual iterations) by calling:

out$params

This will be a matrix with several columns (one for each parameter), and lots of rows (one for each iteration).

I hope this helps!

Cheers,
Owen

messages.body_plain:
Dear Jenni and BaSTA users,

   We just uploaded to the BaSTA webpage a function to produce similar plots from the one in Colchero and Clark (2012). You can find an explanation on how to load it and use it at the end of the "Application" section of the webpage. Please, let us know if it works well.

   Also, we strongly recommend all users to install BaSTA 1.8 from the webpage, which should be available on CRAN in the next few days. It has important bug fixes.

   Best,

   Fernando



Fernando Colchero
Assistant Professor
Department of Mathematics and Computer Science
Max-Planck Odense Center on the Biodemography of Aging
